quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 15 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: In Illinois, a person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Illinois, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while intoxicated.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from them. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. This also gives you space to react to any hazards.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it easier for others to see you.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: Motorcyclists can go through a red light if it doesn't change to green for at least:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may not trigger some traffic lights because of their size. If this happens, wait at least 120 seconds. Then proceed through the red light carefully. You must yield to any other traffic.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help if needed.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Motorcycles may pass on the right:

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the road shoulder.
By riding on the grass if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is clear pavement at least eight feet wide on the right side. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: In Illinois, you can be convicted of DUI:

options.text: Even if your BAC is below the legal limit.
Only if your BAC is 0.08 percent or higher.
Only if you have a crash with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.
Even if you have not been drinking or used any drugs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if your BAC is below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: A BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. However, you can still be convicted of DUI even with a lower BAC if your driving ability is impaired.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire going flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is the usual sign of tire failure.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Take extra care when riding a new motorcycle or one you are not familiar with. Most crashes happen with riders who have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, downshift and ride slowly toward it. Then speed up and ride away.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen at intersections. Stay alert and watch for vehicles that may cross in front of you.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the right side may encourage the other driver to move back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What should riders do about lane position?

options.text: Stay in one lane position at all times.
Change lane positions often to stay alert.
Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
Never ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the best lane position changes too. Pick a position that gives you the most space and lets other drivers see you clearly.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration depends on how much alcohol was consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Height does not affect BAC.
